items.stem: A customer asks about a policy not in the approved knowledge base. Best action?

options.text: Escalate rather than let the model invent an answer
options.rationale: Correct: ungrounded policy answers risk being wrong; escalation protects accuracy.

options.text: Let ChatGPT guess a plausible policy
options.rationale: Inventing policy can mislead customers and create liability.

options.text: Tell the customer the AI is always right
options.rationale: Overclaiming accuracy is unsafe and untrue.
Ignoring the customer fails the service goal.

items.explanation: Correct: ungrounded policy answers risk being wrong; escalation protects accuracy.

items.stem: Before pasting a support ticket into ChatGPT, what should an agent do?

options.text: Remove or mask personal data not needed for the task
options.rationale: Correct: minimising personal data protects customer privacy.
Oversharing personal data creates privacy risk.
Payment data should never be pasted into a consumer tool.
Consumer tools are not automatically safe for personal data.

items.explanation: Correct: minimising personal data protects customer privacy.

items.stem: Which TWO keep AI-assisted support replies consistent and safe? (Select TWO)

options.text: Ground replies in an approved knowledge base
options.rationale: Correct: grounding keeps answers accurate and consistent.

options.text: Use shared templates for common ticket types
options.rationale: Correct: templates standardise structure and tone across agents.

options.text: Let each agent invent policy on the spot
options.rationale: Ad-hoc policy creates inconsistent, risky answers.

options.text: Skip human review on sensitive complaints
options.rationale: Sensitive cases need a human check.

items.explanation: Correct: grounding keeps answers accurate and consistent.
